AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law and the general business law,
in relation to the sale of dogs, cats and rabbits
items.lawCode: Amd §§16, 400 & 408, Ag & Mkts L; amd §752, add §753-f, Gen Bus L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1130

SPONSOR: GIANARIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the agriculture and markets law and the general business
law, in relation to the sale of dogs, cats and rabbits

 
PURPOSE:

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subdivision 48 of section 16 of the agriculture and
markets law to provide training materials in accordance with the other
sections of this act

Section 2 amends subdivision 4 of section 400 of the agriculture and
markets law, adding a new paragraph (d) to include retail pet shops as
defined in subdivision 8 of section 752 of the general business law

Section 3 amends paragraphs (e) and (f) of subdivision 4 of section 408
of the agriculture and markets law, and adds a new paragraph (g) to
allow the department to deny the registration of a non-profit if the
entity was previously licensed as a pet dealer

Section 4 amends the opening paragraph of subdivision 3 of section 752
of the general business law, and a new paragraph (d) is added to clarify
that retail pet shops are not considered pet dealers

Section 5 amends section 752 of the general business law, adding a new
subdivision 8 to define "retail pet shop"

Section 6 amends the general business law, adding a new section 753-f to
prohibit the sale of dogs, cats and rabbits

Section 7 sets the effective date

 
EXISTING LAW:

 
JUSTIFICATION:

At a time where there are healthy and loving pets waiting to be adopted
from animal shelters statewide, there is simply no reason to allow the
sale of puppy mill animals. Puppy mill animals are mistreated from
birth, and often develop behavioral or physical health problems later in
life despite their high price tags. This bill would encourage the
adoption of dogs, cats and rabbits and ensure that animals no longer
have to face the cruelty, physical and psychological abuse-to which the
puppy mill supply chain subjects animals.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: Passed Senate/Died in Agriculture (Assembly)

2019: Died in Domestic Animal Welfare/Died in Agriculture (Assembly)

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None
 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:


 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
One year after it shall have become law

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 40 Chapter 681
 
        MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 1130, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the agriculture and markets law and the general
        business law, in relation to the sale of dogs, cats and rabbits"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would prohibit the sale of dogs, cats and rabbits by  retail
pet  shops.  Retail  pet  shops include any for-profit place of business
that sells or offers for sale animals to be kept as household  pets,  or
pet food or supplies. It does not include breeders who sell animals that
are  born  and  raised on the breeder's residential premises directly to
consumers.
 
  By prohibiting the retail sale of dogs, cats and  rabbits,  this  bill
aims  to shut down a key avenue for the sale of animals that are bred in
unscrupulous "puppy mill" facilities. The Department of Agriculture  and
Markets  (AGM) does not have jurisdiction to oversee facilities that are
not in the State and many of the pets sold in the pet store are from out
of State.
 
  I support the intent of this bill; however, amendments  are  necessary
to  ensure  that  impacted retail pet shops, often small businesses, can
collect rental fees for showing pets available  for  adoption  at  local
shelters  to  provide  AGM  two  years to implement this new law, and to
provide the small businesses impacted by these changes  the  opportunity
to  change  their  business  model. I have secured an agreement with the
Legislature to make these necessary changes.
 
  Based on this agreement, I am signing this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Prohibits the sale of dogs, cats and rabbits by retail pet shops; authorizes collaboration with entities to provide space to showcase cats or dogs owned by certain entities for the purpose of adoption.
